text:
Predicates:
FinancialAid(x, y) ::: x provides y as financial aid.
Applicant(x) ::: x is an applicant for the GRE.
Hardship(x) ::: x proves economic hardship.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x has difficulty caused by having too little money or resources.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(x) ::: x lives in a single-parent family.
DadOutOfWorkMoreThanYear(x) ::: x’s dad has been out of work for more than a year.

Premises:
Cost(GRE, 205) ::: It costs US $205 to take the GRE test.
∀x (FinancialAid(ETS, y) ∧ Applicant(x) → Hardship(x)) ::: ETS provides financial aid to GRE applicants who prove hardship.
EconomicHardship(x) ⇔ difficulty caused by having too little money or resources ::: Economic hardship refers to difficulty caused by having too little money or too few resources.
LivesInSingleParentFamily(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family.
DadOutOfWorkMoreThanYear(tom’s dad) ::: His dad has been out of work for more than a year.

Conclusion:
∃x (FinancialAid(ETS, GRE) ∧ Applicant(x) ∧ Hardship(x)) ::: Tom can apply for financial aid from ETS to take the GRE test.
